motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Hover lifts on buttons and cards (sanctioned exception).

motion.name: reveal-rise
motion.value: translateY(28px) scale(0.985) -> none, view() timeline, 36px stagger, done by 220px
motion.purpose: CSS scroll-driven reveal; never hides content by script; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.purpose: Inertial document scroll; not started under reduced motion; stopped while any <dialog> is open; dialogs and [data-lenis-prevent] scroll natively. No CSS scroll-behavior: smooth.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All ambient loops stop; Lenis stays off; slider switches instantly.

gradients.name: gradient-button
gradients.purpose: Only fill that carries white text/icons (>=5.3:1); filled buttons, logo tile, favicon, chatbot launcher. Same in both themes.

gradients.name: gradient-brand
gradients.purpose: Decorative: section-title highlight words, card hover bar, scrollbar thumb. Day uses #047857 -> #0e7490.

narrative.overview:
The engineer stands at the centre of his own stack, under a cool near-black sky (#05090b) lit by two soft lights: emerald top-left, cyan bottom-right. Content sits on frosted glass panels edged with emerald hairlines; actions are pills; a Three.js constellation of emerald and cyan points drifts behind the page and leans toward the cursor. The palette is the owner's own emerald → cyan identity: two colours, two-stop gradients, nothing else. The layout and motion vocabulary (glass panels, pill controls, spring lifts, gradient last words) was inspired by a reference site; the colour is the owner's.

Dark is the default and the server-rendered theme: `:root, .dark` carry the night tokens, `.light` carries the day tokens (a pale mint ground with deep emerald and deep cyan). `next-themes` runs with `defaultTheme="dark"` and `enableSystem={false}`, so the OS preference is deliberately ignored; the day/night switch in the header is the only way in. Tailwind exposes `dark:` and `light:` custom variants; components are written for night first and use `light:` only where day genuinely differs.

Density is generous: wide sections, short copy, one strong action per block. Motion is inertial smooth scrolling, a spring lift on hover, a staggered rise on scroll, and a slow ambient drift, and all of it stops under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Cool near-black ground with two soft radial glows (`--page-glow`), emerald top-left (11%) and cyan bottom-right (7%), fixed to the viewport.
Two colours only: emerald and cyan. Every gradient has exactly two stops.
Glass panels: 3.5% white fill, 16px blur, emerald hairline borders, 24px corners.
Pill-shaped everything that you press or read as a tag.
Space Grotesk headings with the last words of a section title in the brand gradient.
Real screenshots in a fixed frame, or designed, labelled cover illustrations; never stock imagery.

rules.name: The Two Colours Rule
rules.body: The palette is emerald and cyan, and every gradient has exactly two stops, emerald first. No third hue, no violet, purple, or pink, no three-stop gradients. Error rose is a status colour, not a brand colour.

rules.name: The Deep Stops Rule
rules.body: White text and white icons only ever sit on `--gradient-button` (#047857 → #0e7490). Never put white on `--gradient-brand`; its bright stops fail contrast.

rules.name: The Strong-For-Text Rule
rules.body: A hue used as text uses its `-strong` token (`text-primary-strong`, `text-secondary-strong`, `text-accent-strong`). The base tokens are for fills, glows, and borders.

rules.name: The Brand Exception Rule
rules.body: WhatsApp green (`whatsapp-green`) appears on the floating WhatsApp button and nowhere else. Third-party brand colours stay inside their own marks.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on code, file paths, years, counters, and data values. Never on headings, buttons, or running prose.

rules.name: The Gradient Last Words Rule
rules.body: A section title may end in a `text-gradient` highlight (one phrase, at the end). The hero name uses `text-gradient-display`. No other text is gradient-filled. (Sanctioned detector exception in `.impeccable/config.json`; the utilities are defined once in globals.css.)

rules.name: The Explicit Base Rule
rules.body: Every responsive grid declares `grid-cols-1` (or another explicit count) at the base, and every `fr` track is written `minmax(0,…fr)` so long words, code, or images can never force overflow. Check at 375px.

rules.name: The Lift Rule
rules.body: Interactive surfaces rise on hover (buttons −2px, floating actions −4px, cards −6px) on the spring easing and gain `--shadow-lift`; they return on `:active`. Nothing else moves on hover.

dos: **Do** use semantic token utilities only; the hex values in this file are documentation, `globals.css` is the source.
**Do** keep to emerald and cyan, with two-stop gradients that start on emerald.
**Do** design for night first and add `light:` overrides only where day differs.
**Do** put white text and icons only on `--gradient-button`.
**Do** use the `-strong` token whenever a hue is text.
**Do** give every responsive grid an explicit base column count and wrap `fr` tracks in `minmax(0,…)`.
**Do** show screenshots `object-contain` in a fixed frame (16:10 slider stage, fixed-height lightbox stage) so the frame never jumps.
**Do** build interactive primitives on `<dialog>`, `<details>`, and ARIA patterns in `src/components/ui/`.
**Do** stop every loop and smooth scrolling under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** reintroduce violet, purple, pink, or any third brand hue, or a three-stop gradient.
**Don't** use WhatsApp green anywhere but the WhatsApp button.
**Don't** add shadcn, Radix, or a second dialog/tab/carousel implementation.
**Don't** add CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth`; Lenis owns smooth scrolling.
**Don't** follow the OS colour scheme or make light the default.
**Don't** hide content with JavaScript for reveal effects.
**Don't** gradient-fill text beyond the section-title highlight and the hero name.
**Don't** set headings, buttons, or prose in JetBrains Mono.
**Don't** use stock photos or unlabelled fake screenshots; use real screenshots or a labelled illustration.
**Don't** introduce hard offset shadows or glow colours outside emerald and cyan.
